page.title: What Is a Variable in Python?
page.introduction: Before working with functions, classes, data structures, and other Python concepts, it is important to understand how variables work and how Python associates names with objects.
page.definition: A variable in Python is a name that refers to an object stored in memory.

explanation.content: When Python executes x = 10, the name x becomes associated with an integer object representing the value 10.
A Python variable is therefore better understood as a name binding or reference rather than a box that directly contains a value.
This model becomes especially important when multiple variables refer to the same object or when a variable is reassigned to a different object.

characteristics.title: Name Binding
characteristics.description: A variable name is bound to an object. The name provides a way to access that object during program execution.

characteristics.title: Dynamic Typing
characteristics.description: Python determines the type of an object at runtime. A variable name itself does not have a permanently fixed data type.

characteristics.title: Object Reference
characteristics.description: A variable refers to an object rather than physically containing the object's value.

characteristics.title: Reassignment
characteristics.description: A variable can be rebound to another object during program execution.

characteristics.title: Multiple References
characteristics.description: More than one variable can refer to the same object. Python names and objects are separate concepts.

page.takeaway: The most important idea is that a Python variable is a name bound to an object. Python variables are dynamically typed, can be reassigned, and multiple names can refer to the same object.
